section: Filling performance of an Acid Blue 1 leveler on blind microvias†
text: This work systematically studied the influence of the Acid Blue 1 (AB1) leveler on blind microvia filling. AB1 exhibits excellent suppression during electroplating, with its efect strengthening as the AB1 concentration increases. Chronopotentiometry was used to study the interaction among AB1, SPS, and PEG. There is a synergistic suppressing interaction between the new leveler AB1 and suppressor PEG, while there is competition between AB1 and accelerator SPS.

section: Filling performance of an Acid Blue 1 leveler on blind microvias†
text: There is a synergistic suppressing interaction between the new leveler AB1 and suppressor PEG, while there is competition between AB1 and accelerator SPS. During electrodeposition, AB1 can adsorb on the copper substrate to reduce active sites and suppress copper electrodeposition, based on theoretical studies and in situ infrared spectroscopy. At the optimized electroplating process, void-free microvia filling is achieved with 20 mg/L AB1 and successive electroplating confirms the stability of AB1.

section: Filling performance of an Acid Blue 1 leveler on blind microvias†
text: At the optimized electroplating process, void-free microvia filling is achieved with 20 mg/L AB1 and successive electroplating confirms the stability of AB1. Based on difusion diferences among additives and the competition between AB1 and SPS, a gradient competitive adsorption superfilling mechanism was proposed to illustrate the filling process of the AB1–SPS–PEG system. AB1 is beneficial to improving flatness and lowering surface roughness of the copper layer, which is conducive to reducing signal losses during high-frequency transmission.

text: Blind microvia filling is a key interconnect technology in the manufacturing process of PCBs, allowing for electrical connections between diferent layers in the circuit board. 4,5 The application of this technology enhances PCB design flexibility, enabling more complex circuit layouts and greater space utilization. Copper is widely used as an interconnect line in blind microvias for PCB manufacturing due to its good electronic (thermal and electrical conductivity) and mechanical (wear resistance and elongation, etc.) properties.

section: Filling performance of an Acid Blue 1 leveler on blind microvias† > 1. Introduction
text: Copper is widely used as an interconnect line in blind microvias for PCB manufacturing due to its good electronic (thermal and electrical conductivity) and mechanical (wear resistance and elongation, etc.) properties. 6,7 The filling of blind microvias with copper is achieved through electroplating technology. 8–10 In PCBs, copper not only provides a stable electrical connection but also enhances the structural strength of HDI PCBs, improving heat and wear resistance.

section: Filling performance of an Acid Blue 1 leveler on blind microvias† > 1. Introduction
text: 8–10 In PCBs, copper not only provides a stable electrical connection but also enhances the structural strength of HDI PCBs, improving heat and wear resistance. 11 Moreover, copper interconnect lines effectively reduce losses in signal transmission and enhance signal integrity, which is especially important for high-frequency and high-speed circuits. 12 During copper electroplating, it is essential to adjust the metal deposition process in local microvias to avoid the formation of void defects caused by the edge effect, which can undermine the properties of the copper interconnect layer.

section: Filling performance of an Acid Blue 1 leveler on blind microvias† > 1. Introduction
text: 12 During copper electroplating, it is essential to adjust the metal deposition process in local microvias to avoid the formation of void defects caused by the edge effect, which can undermine the properties of the copper interconnect layer. The most common method is the addition of proper additives. 13–15 The additives used in copper electroplating fall into three categories: accelerators, suppressors, and levelers. 16 The most commonly used accelerator, suppressor, and leveler is bis-(sodium sulfopropyl)- disulfide (SPS), polyethylene glycol (PEG), and Janus Green B (JGB).

section: Filling performance of an Acid Blue 1 leveler on blind microvias† > 1. Introduction
text: 16 The most commonly used accelerator, suppressor, and leveler is bis-(sodium sulfopropyl)- disulfide (SPS), polyethylene glycol (PEG), and Janus Green B (JGB). 17 During electroplating, density functional theory (DFT) calculations, in situ Raman spectroscopy, and scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) studies reveal that the disulfide bond of SPS will break up, with the sulfurcontaining side adsorbing on the copper base, while the other side (containing a sulfonic acid group) captures free Cu ^2 + to accelerate reduction with adsorbed Cl - through the ‘‘bridging efect’’.

section: Filling performance of an Acid Blue 1 leveler on blind microvias† > 1. Introduction
text: 17 During electroplating, density functional theory (DFT) calculations, in situ Raman spectroscopy, and scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) studies reveal that the disulfide bond of SPS will break up, with the sulfurcontaining side adsorbing on the copper base, while the other side (containing a sulfonic acid group) captures free Cu ^2 + to accelerate reduction with adsorbed Cl - through the ‘‘bridging efect’’. 18–20 As for PEG, in situ Raman and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations confirm the formation of PEG-Cu^2+-Cl^- adsorbate complexes, which increase the energy barrier and suppress copper electrodeposition.

section: Filling performance of an Acid Blue 1 leveler on blind microvias† > 1. Introduction
text: 18–20 As for PEG, in situ Raman and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations confirm the formation of PEG-Cu^2+-Cl^- adsorbate complexes, which increase the energy barrier and suppress copper electrodeposition. 21–23 Mass spectrometry (MS) and DFT calculations demonstrate that the azo group of JGB competes with the reduction of Cu ^2 + to obtain electrons, leading to dissociation 24,25 into phenazine derivatives that can also adsorb on active sites to suppress copper growth. 26,27 Among these additives, levelers are key components for achieving defect-free filling in blind vias.

section: Filling performance of an Acid Blue 1 leveler on blind microvias† > 1. Introduction
text: 26,27 Among these additives, levelers are key components for achieving defect-free filling in blind vias. 28 Nowadays, triphenylmethane derivatives are promising levelers and have been used in throughhole and blind-hole filling due to the unlocalized orbital distribution of the tertiary amine structure. 29,30 In this work, a novel triphenylmethane derivative, Acid Blue 1 (AB1), was selected as a potential leveler, and the efects of diferent concentrations of AB1 on copper electroplating were investigated.

section: Filling performance of an Acid Blue 1 leveler on blind microvias† > 1. Introduction
text: In this work, a novel triphenylmethane derivative, Acid Blue 1 (AB1), was selected as a potential leveler, and the efects of diferent concentrations of AB1 on copper electroplating were investigated. The interactions among three diferent types of additives were studied using galvanostatic measurements. The influencing mechanism of AB1 on the copper cathode surface during electroplating was also studied theoretically and experimentally. The filling performance of AB1 in blind microvias was examined, and the electroplating process was optimized.

section: Filling performance of an Acid Blue 1 leveler on blind microvias† > 1. Introduction
text: The filling performance of AB1 in blind microvias was examined, and the electroplating process was optimized. Additionally, the surface morphology and roughness of the copper interconnect layer were analyzed, and finite element simulation was employed to study the high-frequency signal transmission losses influenced by AB1, while phase structure was investigated by XRD.

text: 3.1.3 Chronopotentiometry analysis. It is important to study the interaction among SPS (accelerator), PEG (suppressor), and AB1 (leveler), as it provides a deeper understanding of the filling mechanism in microvias. 45 Traditionally, galvanostatic measurement is applied to study possible interactions by changing the injection order of the three types of additives. Fig. 1c (up) shows the change in cathodic potential after injecting additives into the testing solution. The cathodic potential declines (230 mV) after adding PEG, indicating its suppressing efect.

section: Filling performance of an Acid Blue 1 leveler on blind microvias† > 3.1 Electrochemical analysis
text: The cathodic potential declines (230 mV) after adding PEG, indicating its suppressing efect. Upon introducing AB1, the cathodic potential further decreases (31 mV), suggesting synergistic cooperation between AB1 and PEG. However, after the addition of SPS, the cathodic potential shifts positively (42 mV), indicating the accelerating efect of SPS in the presence of AB1 and PEG.

section: Filling performance of an Acid Blue 1 leveler on blind microvias† > 3.1 Electrochemical analysis
text: However, after the addition of SPS, the cathodic potential shifts positively (42 mV), indicating the accelerating efect of SPS in the presence of AB1 and PEG. By altering the additive injection order, SPS can cause a positive shift of 205 mV in cathodic potential after PEG injection, suggesting that SPS can replace PEG to accelerate copper electrodeposition, consistent with previous work. 46 Following AB1 injection, the cathodic potential changes negatively (-191 mV).

text: 3.3.1 Electroplating performance. The optimization of the electroplating process is shown in Fig. 3, with the used devices illustrated in Fig. 3c. Without AB1, the growth rate at the opening area is higher than that at the bottom and side walls, leading to void defects in microvias with both diameters (125 mm and 150 mm). At an AB1 concentration of 10 mg L ^- 1, the growth rate at the opening area decreases due to AB1 adsorption, which suppresses copper growth.

text: Coupled with the interactions among the three additives discussed in Section 3.1.3, namely the competition between AB1 and SPS, as well as cooperation between AB1 and PEG, gradient competitive adsorption superfilling was proposed to illustrate the AB1–SPS–PEG system, with a schematic diagram shown in Fig. 3d. At the initial stage (3d1), different additives are distributed uniformly within the microvias. As the filling process progresses (3d2), a concentration gradient for the additives forms due to their consumption and local diffusion transport limitations within the microvias.

section: Filling performance of an Acid Blue 1 leveler on blind microvias† > 3.4 Efect of AB1 on the copper layer
text: 3.4.1 Efect of AB1 on morphology. Fig. 4 and 5a show the surface morphology of the copper layer observed by SEM and Olympus conformal laser microscope. 53 Small bump particles are present on the uneven copper surface electrodeposited without AB1. After introducing 10 mg L ^ - 1 AB1, the surface flatness improves greatly, and the copper layer becomes compact, although large bump morphology remains. As the AB1 concentration continues to rise, the flatness of the copper layer further improves.

section: Filling performance of an Acid Blue 1 leveler on blind microvias† > 3.4 Efect of AB1 on the copper layer
text: As the AB1 concentration continues to rise, the flatness of the copper layer further improves. Using the Olympus conformal laser microscope, the surface roughness ( R _ z) was calculated, as shown in Fig. 5b. R _ z is 128 nm for the copper layer obtained without AB1 and decreases to 92 nm with 10 mg L ^ - 1 AB1. Furthermore, R _ z values obtained from 20 mg L ^ - 1 and 30 mg L ^ - 1 are 83 nm and 75 nm, respectively. The above analysis indicates that AB1 has a micro-scale leveling efect.

text: 3.4.2 Efect of AB1 on signal loss. The influence of AB1 on signal loss during high-frequency transmission was studied using finite element simulation. 54 Fig. 5c shows that signal loss is influenced by surface roughness and applied frequency. Total loss increases with rising frequency and R _z. Additionally, the total loss with frequency for the copper layer obtained with JGB is also calculated (Fig. S5d, ESI†). In comparison, the signal loss obtained with AB1 is smaller than with JGB at the same frequency due to a lower R _z for AB1.

section: Filling performance of an Acid Blue 1 leveler on blind microvias† > 4. Conclusion
text: A novel leveler, Acid Blue 1, was used to achieve void-free copper filling in blind microvias. Electrochemical tests (CV and EIS) confirm the suppressive efect on the reduction of Cu ^2 +. During copper electroplating, there is a synergistic suppression between AB1 and PEG, but competition between AB1 and SPS. DFT calculations and in situ infrared spectroscopy provide a deeper understanding of AB1 adsorption configuration on the copper substrate during electrodeposition, indicating that AB1 can reduce active sites and act as a barrier adsorption layer to increase cathodic polarization.

section: Filling performance of an Acid Blue 1 leveler on blind microvias† > 4. Conclusion
text: DFT calculations and in situ infrared spectroscopy provide a deeper understanding of AB1 adsorption configuration on the copper substrate during electrodeposition, indicating that AB1 can reduce active sites and act as a barrier adsorption layer to increase cathodic polarization. After electroplating optimization, microvias with diameters of 125 mm and 150 mm can be filled with 20 mg L^-1 AB1 at 1.5 Adm ^- 2; the good stability of AB1 indicates its industrial potential.

section: Filling performance of an Acid Blue 1 leveler on blind microvias† > 4. Conclusion
text: After electroplating optimization, microvias with diameters of 125 mm and 150 mm can be filled with 20 mg L^-1 AB1 at 1.5 Adm ^- 2; the good stability of AB1 indicates its industrial potential. A gradient competitive adsorption superfilling mechanism was proposed to explain the filling process for the AB1–SPS–PEG system. The diffusion differences among the three additives and the competition between AB1 and SPS are key to achieving bottom-up growth in microvias.

section: Filling performance of an Acid Blue 1 leveler on blind microvias† > 4. Conclusion
text: The diffusion differences among the three additives and the competition between AB1 and SPS are key to achieving bottom-up growth in microvias. AB1 improves the copper layer quality, enhances surface flatness, refines the grains, and reduces signal losses during high-frequency transmission. Additionally, AB1 suppresses the formation of Cu(220) while promoting the formation of Cu(111) and Cu(200).
